## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.
data.title: Engine game-outcome surface and cross-game meta-achievements

# Goal

As a game developer depending on the engine, I want a core-owned, exported
renderer-aware container clip so a WebGL boot clips panel content exactly like a
Canvas boot does — and downstream repos stop carrying their own copies.

Port the proven pattern from `../tce-main-street/src/ContainerClip.ts`
(do **not** re-invent it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Core helper.** A renderer-aware container-clip helper exists in core, exported
  through the public `@ui` surface with the `ContainerClip` API (`setRect`,
  `clear`, `destroy`) and the Canvas/WebGL branching described below.
- **WebGL browser test.** At least one browser test forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and
  asserts clipping actually happens (pixel probe via `renderer.snapshotPixel()`)
  and that no `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning is emitted from core
  code; Canvas parity is asserted in the same file.
- `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts` exports `createContainerClip(scene, target, rect?)`
  and the `ContainerClip` interface (`renderer`, `graphics`, `geometryMask`,
  `maskFilter`, `rect`, `active`, `setRect`, `clear`, `destroy`), plus
  `isWebGLRenderer(scene)`; both are exported from `src/ui/index.ts` so
  downstream repos import them from `@ui`.
- Canvas branch keeps today's behaviour: transparent-fill `GeometryMask`,
  Graphics on the display list, `clearMask()` on `clear()` — Canvas rendering
  output is unchanged.
- WebGL branch: `target.enableFilters()` then
  `target.filters.internal.addMask(graphics, false, scene.cameras.main)`; the
  mask Graphics is created with `scene.make.graphics(..., false)` (**off** the
  display list) and drawn **opaque**; a missing filter list (no WebGL context)
  degrades to `maskFilter === null` without throwing.
- `clear()` is a real "no clip" on both renderers, and `destroy()` is
  idempotent and removes the filter / mask resources.
- The module doc comment records the Phaser 4 (`4.0.0-rc.7`) restriction —
  `GameObject.setMask` logs "not supported in WebGL" and no-ops — and why the
  mask must be opaque and off the display list.
- Unit tests (`tests/ui/ContainerClip.test.ts`) cover renderer branch selection,
  `clear()`/`destroy()` idempotence and post-destroy no-ops, using stubs.
- Browser test (`tests/ui/ContainerClip.browser.test.ts`), written **before**
  the helper (TDD): under `Phaser.WEBGL` a clipped container's content is
  visible inside the rect and absent outside it (`renderer.snapshotPixel()`
  probe), the result is unchanged when the container is translated (screen-space
  mask), **and no** `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning is captured;
  the same file asserts Canvas parity (clip applied via `GeometryMask`).

## Key Files

- `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts`
- `src/ui/index.ts`
- `tests/ui/ContainerClip.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/ContainerClip.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/helpers/bootRendererScene.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by `CG-0MVTQ3UFI009LH8Q` (WebGL clip test harness).

## Deliverables

- Helper + exports + unit tests + WebGL/Canvas browser parity test green;
  `npm run build` green.
data.title: Core ContainerClip helper: renderer-aware clipping exported from @ui

# Intake Brief: Pretty-print game events in the Game Events debug overlay — CG-0MVTTR0OC006PWDK

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Stage: intake_complete** | **Open questions: 0 (3 resolved by producer, 2026-10-29)**

> Pretty-print each Game Events payload as indented, multi-line JSON inside the debug overlay and never soft-wrap it horizontally, so a full event payload is readable without leaving the game.

**Original request (verbatim):** *"In the game events view of the debug options under the settings menu pretty print the JSON output, do not let it wrap horizontally."*

## Problem Statement

The **Game Events** debug tool (Settings → Debug Tools → Game Events) renders every event as a single line of raw JSON truncated at 80 characters and clipped at the overlay edge. Real payloads (e.g. `state-settled`, `card:placed`, game-specific events) are objects with several keys, so the developer sees a fragment of the first key and cannot read the event at all — the overlay's whole purpose (inspecting event flow and payloads during play) is defeated.

## Users

- **Producer / engine developer (primary):** inspects event payloads while debugging gameplay, event wiring, and replay behaviour.
  - *"As a producer, I want each emitted event's payload shown as indented, readable JSON so I can diagnose an event-driven bug without opening the browser devtools."*
- **Game developer working in a sibling `tce-<game>` repo (secondary):** confirms the exact payload shape a game emits for its own augmented `GameEventMap` events.
  - *"As a game developer, I want to read the full payload of a game-specific event so I can confirm the shape my scene emits."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Full payload pretty-printed.** Each buffered event's payload is rendered as indented multi-line JSON (`JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2)`) under a one-line header of `timestamp [eventName]`. The current 80-character truncation is removed: the entire payload appears in the rendered output (no silent data loss).
2. **No horizontal soft-wrapping.** Payload lines are never word-wrapped; each pretty-printed JSON line is rendered as exactly one line (no `wordWrap` on the text objects).
3. **Nothing is hidden at the right edge.** Lines wider than the dialog's content area are fully reachable rather than clipped mid-glyph (confirmed approach: opt-in horizontal scrolling on the shared overlay dialog, default off — see Appendix Q1). Vertical scrolling and `refresh(totalContentHeight)` clamping keep working, and the two scroll axes do not interfere.
4. **Non-serialisable payloads degrade safely.** `undefined`, `null`, primitives, and circular structures render without throwing, using a documented fallback (e.g. `String(payload)`); a circular payload must not break rendering of the remaining events.
5. **Existing overlay behaviour is preserved.** Clear, Pause/Resume, the 500 ms poll, the event count, the buffer-status text, the `hudContainer` parenting (no content behind the dialog box), and the close/cleanup path all behave as they do today.
6. **Formatting is pure and unit-tested.** The formatting logic is extracted into a Phaser-free helper that is unit-tested for: nested objects and arrays, primitives, `undefined`, an empty object, a circular reference, multi-line output shape, and the absence of truncation. A browser test (or an equivalent deterministic Phaser-level test) verifies the rendered result: multi-line text present, no wrap configured, and the scroll content height grows with the payload line count.
7. **Build and targeted suites pass.** `npm run build` succeeds and the unit and browser suites covering `src/ui/debug` and `src/ui/Overlay.ts` pass; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
8. **Documentation updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments/JSDoc, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Debug Tools → Game Events, and the overlay-dialog scroll contract if the shared dialog changes), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Single source of rendering:** the change lands in the core debug tool (`src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`), so every game composing the engine inherits it; no per-game copies.
- **Shared-component safety:** `src/ui/Overlay.ts` (`createOverlayDialog`) is used by many overlays (state inspector, AI decisions, session export, card packs, parameterised overlays). Any new capability there must be **opt-in with unchanged defaults**, and existing overlay tests must keep passing.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- **Verification commands (copy-paste ready):** `npm run build`; `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/debug/`; `npx vitest run --project browser tests/ui/debug/`; `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/Overlay.test.ts`.
- **Dev-mode only:** the tool remains registered only in dev mode (`isDevMode()`), so the production build is unaffected.
- **Reduced-motion / accessibility unchanged:** no animation is introduced; existing text colours and the monospace content font are retained.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts` — renders one `scene.add.text` per event at a 22 px row pitch, `fontSize: '13px'`, `fontFamily: overlay.monoFont`, **no** `wordWrap`. The line text is `${timestamp} [${eventName}] ${truncatePayload(payload, 80)}`, where `truncatePayload` calls `JSON.stringify` and slices to 80 characters (`…` appended). Because the scroll container is masked to `contentWidth` (`boxWidth - 20`, i.e. 660 px at the 680 px default box), anything past the edge is clipped.
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts` — `createOverlayDialog` provides a modal backdrop, title, close button, a masked `scrollContainer`, and vertical scrolling only (`handle.scrollY`, bounds-checked `wheel` handler, `refresh(totalContentHeight)` clamps and re-applies the geometry mask). The wheel handler already receives `dx`/`dy` from Phaser but ignores `dx`.
- `src/ui/debug/GlobalEventBuffer.ts` — singleton holding `{ timestamp, eventName, payload }` entries with the **raw** payload, so no information is lost before rendering; the overlay is the only place that truncates.
- Precedents: `src/ui/debug/StateInspectorOverlay.ts` word-wraps its tree text (`wordWrap: { width: … }`); `src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts` already serialises with `JSON.stringify(…, null, 2)`; `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the Game Events tool as a "truncated view of the event payload".

## Desired Change

1. **Extract a pure formatter** (new module, e.g. `src/ui/debug/formatEventLog.ts`) exposing a function that turns one buffered event into the rendered string (a one-line header, then the 2-space-indented JSON body) plus a helper that reports the widest rendered line width, with a safe JSON serialiser that falls back on circular/unsupported values.
2. **Render multi-line, unwrapped text:** one text object per event (header + pretty JSON joined with newlines, `lineSpacing` set, no `wordWrap`) so the object count stays proportional to the event count rather than the JSON line count; recompute `refresh(totalContentHeight)` from the aggregated text heights.
3. **Make wide lines reachable** via the confirmed opt-in horizontal scroll (`scrollX` in `OverlayDialogHandle`, clamped to the measured widest line, opt-in option on `createOverlayDialog`, defaults unchanged), requested only by the Game Events overlay.
4. **Update the docs** (Debug Tools → Game Events feature bullets; overlay-dialog scroll contract if the shared dialog gains an option) and keep the tool's `description` string accurate if the behaviour summary changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts` — Render each event as a header line plus pretty-printed payload; drop `truncatePayload`; request horizontal scroll when needed.
- `src/ui/debug/formatEventLog.ts` — **New**: pure, Phaser-free event/payload formatting helpers (pretty JSON, safe serialisation, widest-line measurement).
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts` — Optional opt-in horizontal scrolling on `createOverlayDialog` (`scrollX` on the handle, `dx` handling in the existing wheel handler, clamping in `refresh`); defaults unchanged.
- `src/ui/debug/index.ts` — Re-export the new formatter if it is part of the debug-tools surface.
- `tests/ui/debug/AiDecisionOverlay.test.ts` — Reference pattern for a non-Phaser debug-overlay unit test (do not change unless shared code forces it).
- `tests/ui/debug/formatEventLog.test.ts` — **New**: unit tests for pretty printing, no truncation, primitive/`undefined`/circular handling, widest-line measurement.
- `tests/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.test.ts` — **New**: rendering-level test (text content contains the pretty JSON and spans multiple lines; no wrap; scroll height grows).
- `tests/ui/Overlay.test.ts` — Extend for the opt-in horizontal scroll (clamping, default-off behaviour, mask/refresh interaction).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Debug Tools → Game Events bullets; overlay-dialog scroll contract.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Shared overlay regression.** Adding horizontal scrolling to `createOverlayDialog` touches a component used by ~10 overlays. *Mitigation:* opt-in option with unchanged defaults; the existing `Overlay.test.ts` suite must pass untouched; add explicit default-off coverage.
- **Rendering cost with long sessions.** Pretty JSON multiplies rendered lines; a 1,000-event buffer of large payloads could produce very tall content and heavy text objects. *Mitigation:* one text object per event (not per JSON line) keeps object count equal to the event count, matching today's cost; if profiling shows a problem, cap the rendered window (most recent N) in a follow-up rather than widening this item's scope.
- **Widest-line measurement drift.** Estimating widths from character counts can mis-clamp horizontal scroll. *Mitigation:* measure the rendered text object's `width` (Phaser text metrics) after creation and use the maximum.
- **Scope creep.** Tempting extras (per-event expand/collapse, JSON syntax colouring, copy-to-clipboard, search/filter, the AI Decision overlay's payloads) are recorded as separate work items rather than added here.

### Assumptions

- The overlay is the only place payloads are truncated; `GlobalEventBuffer` already retains full payloads (verified in `src/ui/debug/GlobalEventBuffer.ts`).
- The tool is dev-only, so no production bundle impact needs to be argued.
- Pretty printing the **payload** (with a compact `timestamp [eventName]` header) is the confirmed scope; the whole-record and expand/collapse variants are out of scope (Appendix Q2).
- The overlay's default 680 px box (`Math.min(GAME_W - 80, 680)` at the 1280 × 720 design viewport) stays as-is; wide lines are handled by horizontal scrolling rather than by widening the box (Appendix Q1).
- The dialog stays modal: scrolling remains bounds-checked to the dialog box so wheel input never leaks to overlays beneath it.

## Related Work

- **Game Event Log debug tool (CG-0MS1QC3KR004C7UQ)** [completed]: introduced the Game Events overlay, `GlobalEventBuffer`, and the 80-character `truncatePayload` rendering this item replaces. This item is its direct enhancement follow-up.
- **State inspector overlay with filter (CG-0MS1QC3E1003G5S4)** [completed]: sibling debug overlay; uses `wordWrap` on tree text — the precedent this item deliberately does **not** follow for payload lines (no wrapping allowed).
- **AI Decision Viewer debug tool (CG-0MS1QC4SC006FPFM)** [completed]: sibling overlay with the same one-text-object-per-record rendering; a candidate follow-up if payload readability is wanted there too (out of scope — see Risks → scope creep).
- **Detect when running in developer mode and provide debug tools (CG-0MQZYFG3C0063DN3)** [completed]: established the dev-mode-only registration path the tool still uses.
- **Documentation update for dev mode debug tools (CG-0MS1QBONV0082TIQ)** [completed]: the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` Debug Tools section that AC8 updates.
- **Main Street business hand / Package config items (CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD, CG-0MLSGNJUD0F48DHV)**: returned by the automated keyword sweep only (shared words such as "game"/"json"); **not related** and excluded from scope.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MS1QC3KR004C7UQ** – Game Event Log debug tool (completed)
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** – Main Street: merge business hand + held event into one horizontal 3-card hand (completed)
- **CG-0MLSGNJUD0F48DHV** – Package.json, Vite, and TypeScript Config (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: debug, events, game, json, let (+8 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: debug, events, game, json, let (+6 more)
- `README.md` — matched: debug, events, game, json, let (+6 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1 (horizontal overflow handling, resolved).** Q: "How should pretty-printed lines that are wider than the dialog be handled? **(A)** *Recommended* — add opt-in horizontal scrolling to the shared overlay dialog so every line stays on one line and is fully readable; (B) keep vertical-only scrolling and elide over-wide lines with `…`; (C) widen the dialog to near-full width and shrink the font, still clipping anything longer." — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): **(A) — opt-in horizontal scrolling on the shared overlay dialog, default off.** Source: interactive reply to comment CG-C0MVU2ZWN10087W81. **Recommended and accepted:** (A) — it is the only option that satisfies both "pretty-print" and "do not wrap" without hiding payload data. Evidence: `src/ui/Overlay.ts` (`createOverlayDialog` has vertical-only scrolling; the wheel handler already receives `dx`).
- **Q2 (pretty-print scope, resolved).** Q: "What exactly should be pretty-printed? **(A)** *Recommended* — the payload only, under a one-line `timestamp [eventName]` header; (B) the whole event record (`{ timestamp, eventName, payload }`) as JSON; (C) payload plus a per-event expand/collapse toggle." — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): **(A) — pretty-print the payload only, under a one-line `timestamp [eventName]` header.** Source: interactive reply to comment CG-C0MVU2ZWN10087W81. (A) keeps the existing one-line-per-event scanning behaviour and adds no interaction. Evidence: current line format in `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`; `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents "ISO timestamp, event name, and a truncated view of the event payload".
- **Q3 (buffer size behaviour, resolved).** Q: "Should the overlay keep rendering every buffered event, or cap the rendered window? **(A)** *Recommended* — keep rendering all events (no behavioural change beyond formatting); (B) render only the most recent N events with a 'showing last N' note." — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): **(A) — keep rendering every buffered event.** Source: interactive reply to comment CG-C0MVU2ZWN10087W81. **Recommended and accepted:** (A) — a cap is a separate performance decision and would hide history the producer may need.
- Q: "Is the target the dev-mode Settings → Debug Tools → **Game Events** overlay only, or also game-owned activity logs (e.g. Main Street)?" — Answer (derived from the item text: "the game events view of the debug options under the settings menu"): the Game Events debug tool only. Evidence: `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (§ Debug Tools → Game Events). Source: work-item description + repo search (no interview required).
- Q: "Are payloads already retained in full anywhere?" — Answer: yes — `GlobalEventBuffer` stores the raw payload; truncation happens only at render time. Evidence: `src/ui/debug/GlobalEventBuffer.ts` (`payload: unknown`, pushed unmodified). Research: repo inspection, no buffer-level truncation found.
- Q: "Is an existing pretty-print helper available for reuse?" — Answer: no shared helper; `src/ui/debug/SessionExportTool.ts` inlines `JSON.stringify(…, null, 2)`, so a small shared formatter is extracted here. Research: `grep 'null, 2'` in `src/` returns only `SessionExportTool.ts` and `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts`.

data.description:
## Goal

Update the developer documentation so the pretty-printed Game Events overlay and the shared overlay dialog's scroll contract are documented where developers look for them.

## Scope

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` → **Debug Tools → Game Events**:
  - Replace the "truncated view of the event payload" bullet with: each event renders a one-line `timestamp [eventName]` header plus the full payload as indented (2-space) JSON, no truncation, no word wrap.
  - Document that wide lines are reachable by scrolling horizontally (opt-in on the shared dialog) and that vertical scrolling still applies.
  - Keep the existing live-feed / Clear / Pause-Resume / `window.__GAME_EVENTS__` bullets accurate; update the `Implementation:` line if the formatter module is worth naming.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` → overlay/shared-UI documentation: a short **overlay dialog scroll contract** note — `createOverlayDialog` is vertical-only by default, `enableHorizontalScroll: true` opts in, `refresh(totalContentHeight, totalContentWidth)` drives both clamps, and the mask stays fixed while the container translates.
- Add a brief mention in the AGENTS.md Gym/scene guidance **only if** it already documents overlay behaviour that is now stale; otherwise leave AGENTS.md untouched (do not edit agent-infrastructure files).
- Do **not** edit `CHANGELOG.md` (release pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Documentation updated to reflect the changes — Debug Tools → Game Events in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` describes pretty-printed, untruncated, unwrapped payloads and the horizontal-scroll affordance, plus the overlay-dialog scroll contract for the shared dialog, code comments/JSDoc, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Docs/DEVELOPER.md documents the overlay-dialog scroll contract for the shared dialog (`enableHorizontalScroll` default off, `refresh(totalContentHeight, totalContentWidth)` clamping, fixed mask, translating container).
- [ ] Code comments/JSDoc landed by the implementation items are cross-referenced from the docs where useful (formatter module name, option name).
- [ ] Docs contain no stale claim that payloads are truncated, and use UK English.
- [ ] Build and targeted suites pass: `npm run build` succeeds (docs-only change must not break the build).

## Verification

- `npm run build`.
- Read-back check of the edited sections: `grep -n "Game Events" -A 20 docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Key Files

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`

**Parent:** CG-0MVTTR0OC006PWDK — AC8, AC7
